# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes managing public finances to reduce national debt as a share of GDP while investing in infrastructure. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding the British Business Bank, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The party would reform capital gains tax, increase the Digital Services Tax to 6%, and introduce a 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks. Employment reforms include creating a "dependent contractor" status with basic rights, higher minimum wage for zero-hour contracts, and expanded sick pay eligibility.

## Health and Social Care
The manifesto commits to 8,000 additional GPs to enable seven-day appointment guarantees, expanded NHS dentistry access, and mental health hubs in every community. Cancer treatment would have a 62-day guarantee from referral. Social care would include free personal care based on the Scottish model, a new Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour above standard), and a cross-party commission on sustainable funding. Unpaid carers would receive increased Carer's Allowance and statutory respite breaks.

## Climate and Energy
Targets include net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home insulation programme would prioritise low-income households. The party would remove restrictions on solar and wind development, invest in grid infrastructure and energy storage, and implement a Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. Water companies would be transformed into public benefit companies with sewage discharge bans.

## Education
Proposals include a qualified mental health professional in every school, above-inflation funding increases, and a tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils. Early years would see extra free hours for disadvantaged three and four-year-olds. University maintenance grants would be reinstated. Teacher recruitment would be addressed through workforce strategy and reformed pay review processes.

## Housing and Communities
The target is 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through garden cities and reformed land compensation rules. Renters would receive three-year default tenancies and no-fault eviction bans. Leasehold would be abolished. Local authorities would gain powers over second homes and short-term lets, including council tax increases up to 500%.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto would repeal the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme while establishing safe legal routes for refugees. Asylum seekers could work after three months. Work visa policy would transfer from the Home Office to relevant departments. Family visa income thresholds would be reversed, and the Youth Mobility Scheme expanded to age 35.

## Political Reform
Electoral changes include proportional representation via Single Transferable Vote for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, and scrapping voter ID requirements. The Ministerial Code would become statutory. House of Lords reform would introduce democratic mandate. Donation caps would apply to political parties.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP with Army cuts reversed. The nuclear deterrent would be maintained. European cooperation would deepen through a four-stage roadmap toward Single Market membership. International development would return to 0.7% of national income with a restored independent department.
